notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 12/19/2025
Patient: Sasha Wilkinson, 65-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 12/19/2025. The study demonstrated significant sleep-disordered breathing. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 42.0 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 11% of all events. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent desaturations associated with respiratory events. Sleep architecture was fragmented with reduced REM sleep. These findings indicate severe sleep apnea with a notable proportion of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and consideration of therapeutic interventions are recommended.

Sleep Medicine Consultation Note
Date: 07/21/2026
Patient: Sasha Wilkinson, 66-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of obstructive sleep apnea with CPAP therapy.

History:
Ms. Wilkinson has been using CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. She reports consistent nightly use but continues to experience symptoms suggestive of inadequate control.

Physical Examination:
BMI 26.3 kg/m2.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 18.5 events/hour on CPAP at 13 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
Persistent obstructive sleep apnea despite adherence to CPAP therapy at adequate pressure settings.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options including bilevel positive airway pressure or advanced PAP modalities.
2. Evaluate for potential upper airway resistance or other contributing factors.
3. Schedule follow-up sleep study to reassess efficacy of therapy.
4. Continue monitoring adherence and symptoms.

Summary:
Ms. Wilkinson demonstrates CPAP failure with significant residual apnea events despite compliance. Further evaluation and treatment adjustment are warranted to improve sleep quality and reduce apnea burden.
